findings.summary: A new Windows infostealer called VOLTA does more than steal passwords. After it grabs Gmail, Discord and other logins, it asks an AI model to study the loot and write a report on how much the victim is worth. The idea is simple: steal everything, then let AI sort it out. The malware calls itself “VOLTA-AUTODOXER.” It deletes itself after running, which makes it harder to find. It is also a sign of where cybercrime is heading.
findings.title: VOLTA Malware Steals Gmail and Discord Sessions, Then Uses AI to Build Detailed Victim Profiles

The fix arrived in two stages.

findings.summary: ### Summary Elo's programmatic AST API accepts arbitrary values in many node fields without runtime type or syntax validation. Each backend's emit stage interpolates those values straight into the generated source with no escape pass. An integrator that populates the AST from JSON-deserialised input, plugin output, or any other untyped source therefore exposes a code-injection primitive that flows through to the emitted JavaScript, Ruby, Python, or SQL.
findings.title: Elo backends have code injection via unvalidated emission of programmatic AST fields

findings.summary: ### Summary An unauthenticated attacker who controls a string passed to any Elo JavaScript-emission path — `defaultFormats.elo.parse()`, the `bin/elo` CLI, or the live browser playground at `elo-lang.org/try` — can execute arbitrary code in the host JavaScript runtime.
findings.title: Elo JavaScript emitter has sandbox escape to arbitrary Node.js / browser code execution via unfiltered `.constructor` member access

findings.summary: ### Summary Elo's Ruby backend emits attacker-controlled text into Ruby double-quoted strings without escaping the `#` character.
findings.title: Elo Ruby backend has Remote Code Execution via unescaped `#{...}` interpolation in emitted string literals and subtype-constraint labels

findings.summary: ## TL;DR Loading an attacker-supplied lemma `.pt` runs arbitrary code as the loading user. Since 1.14.0 the lemmatizer stores `pos_dict` as a gzip-compressed pickle in the checkpoint's `dicts` field (a `bytes` value). `torch.load(weights_only=True)` treats `bytes` as a primitive and passes it through unexamined, so its allowlist never sees the inner stream. `Trainer.load` then feeds those bytes to an **unrestricted `pickle.loads`**: the only bare `pickle.loads` in the tree.
findings.title: Stanza: RCE via pickle deserialization in the lemmatizer

Researchers say APT29, also known as Midnight Blizzard or Cozy Bear, planted hidden code on real and cloned sites in the US, Ukraine, the Czech Republic and Bulgaria. Visitors with out-of-date iPhones or Android phones can lose cookies, Wi-Fi passwords and, in some cases, almost all of their phone data. They only need to open the page. The campaign was found in mid-October 2026.

findings.summary: One of the early web application vulnerabilities I remember was CVE-2000-0411 [CVE]. This was a simple vulnerability in a CGI-bin script used to send e-mail. The vulnerability was pretty straightforward: Adding additional parameters to the URL leaked environment variables. Other vulnerabilities allowed setting the "To" address and were heavily abused by spammers. And if parameters were passed directly to the sendmail binary, similar vulnerabilities could allow arbitrary code execution.
findings.title: The Classics Return: Vulnerable E-Mail Scripts, (Wed, Nov 4th)

findings.summary: SolarWinds has warned about a critical command injection flaw in its Dameware remote support software. It is tracked as CVE-2026-28336 and carries a severity score of 9.9 out of 10. The bug could let an attacker take over a computer that an IT team is controlling remotely. Dameware is widely used by help desks and administrators to connect to and fix remote computers. Since the tool runs with strong access, a flaw in it is risky for any company that depends on it.
findings.title: Critical SolarWinds Dameware Flaw Could Allow Attackers to Compromise Remote Systems

findings.summary: Russia-aligned hackers tracked as Gorbag are exploiting a WinRAR vulnerability to steal browser credentials, VPN configurations, and sensitive documents from Ukrainian organizations. Active since at least February 2025, the group targets government agencies, law enforcement bodies, justice institutions, local administrations near the front line, and defense organizations. The campaign favors quick data theft over extended remote control.
findings.title: Gorbag Hackers Exploit WinRAR Vulnerability to Steal Credentials From Ukrainian Government Agencies

findings.summary: Introduction to BOD 26-04 On June 10, 2026, CISA issued Binding Operational Directive 26-04, "Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk." Strip away the regulatory language and it reads like a single operational fact: for a vulnerability that is actively exploited, publicly reachable, and grants an attacker full control, you now have three calendar days to remediate it — and you must run a forensic investigation in parallel to determine whether you've already been breached.
findings.title: The Race Against the 3-Day Clock: How Rapid7 Helps Meet BOD 26-04 Compliance

findings.summary: A vulnerability in the authorization mechanism of Cisco Identity Services Engine (ISE) and Cisco ISE Passive Identity Connector (ISE-PIC) could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to obtain an endpoint identity certificate. This vulnerability is due to improper authorization checks. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted request to an affected device. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to bypass authorization to obtain an endpoint certificate.
findings.title: Cisco Identity Services Engine Authorization Bypass Vulnerability

findings.summary: A vulnerability in the web-based management interface of Cisco UCS Central Software could allow an authenticated, remote attacker to achieve remote code execution or conduct information disclosure attacks on an affected device. This vulnerability is due to insufficient validation of user-supplied input in an HTTP request. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted HTTP request to an affected endpoint on an affected device.
findings.title: Cisco UCS Central Software Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

findings.summary: A newly disclosed bug in APT, the package manager behind Debian and Ubuntu, can let a network spy swap a trusted software package for a bad one. The flaw is tracked as CVE-2026-109518 and can end in code running with root rights, the highest level of control on a Linux system. Debian announced the issue on November 4, 2026, and credited researcher Max Justicz with finding it. APT checks each package against signed data before it installs anything.
findings.title: Debian APT Flaw Lets Hackers Hijack Software Updates and Execute Code as Root

findings.summary: A critical flaw in Ruby on Rails Active Storage lets an unauthenticated user upload a crafted image and make the server write files. If uploads use the Disk service, the same upload can make the server read files too. The Rails team rated the bug Critical, with a CVSS score of 9.8, and published the advisory on November 4, 2026. The flaw has no CVE ID yet. The flaw comes from how ImageMagick works. It picks a coder (a file format handler) based on what is inside a file, not on its name.
findings.title: Critical Ruby on Rails Flaw Could Let Hackers Steal Server Secrets Through Malicious Image Uploads

findings.summary: A macOS malware family called Phexia is spreading through fake web pages that talk Mac users into pasting a command into Terminal. Once the command runs, the malware quietly settles on the Mac, steals the login password, and copies browser data, keychain files, and password-manager extension data. The trick is known as ClickFix. A page shows a fake verification or fix, and the user performs the dangerous step themselves. No software flaw is needed, so the usual protections have little to catch.
findings.title: Hackers Trick Mac Users Into Running Terminal Commands That Install Phexia Password-Stealing Malware

The analysis began on August 12, 2026, when an APK collected in the wild crashed the lab’s test emulators. The file was a banking dropper that never ran.

findings.summary: ### Summary A guest can mount another guest's custom storage volume over `/dev/lxd` and read or write its contents without owning it. The DevLXD storage API blocks access to volumes you don't own, but the instance device-update path that attaches a volume to a container without checks ownership.
findings.title: lxd allows Cross-guest volume hijack via DevLXD device patch

findings.summary: ### Summary kaniko before v1.25.20 can send a Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) access token for Azure Resource Manager to a registry host an attacker controls. A Dockerfile that references an image on a lookalike host, such as `FROM x.azurecr.io.attacker.com/img`, is enough. The build needs no `RUN` instruction and never has to push. The flaw is in the Azure Container Registry (ACR) credential helper, `github.com/chrismellard/docker-credential-acr-env`.
findings.title: kaniko can send the build's Azure (Entra ID) access token to lookalike ACR registry hosts

findings.summary: ## Summary `banks` parses `Tool` JSON objects from the rendered body of `{% completion %}` blocks and later resolves their `import_path` field through `importlib.import_module(...)` + `getattr(...)` to obtain the callable that handles a tool call. There is no allowlist or sanitization on `import_path`, so any importable Python attribute (e.g. `os.system`, `subprocess.getoutput`) can be selected.
findings.title: Banks: Unsafe importlib.import_module of attacker-controlled Tool.import_path in CompletionExtension allows RCE
